elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: New Section 12.3(f): "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, RevMed shall..." — covers both expiry and any termination, and is not limited to a Change-of-Control or Termination Product scenario.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause provides assistance "for a period of at least ninety (90) days"; there is no six-month (or longer) assistance period. To reach preferred, change to "for a period of up to six (6) months following such expiration or termination".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3(f) is silent on pricing for the assistance; no "at RevMed's then-current rates" (or any charging basis) appears. Preferred requires an express rate anchor.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall, within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to Sanofi all data and materials of Sanofi then in RevMed's possession or control" — 30-day clock runs from expiry/termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: No format requirement in the inserted sentence; the only electronic-format reference is in 12.3(c)(vi)C, which runs from Sanofi to RevMed. Add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification obligation was inserted. Section 11.6 only requires destruction of Confidential Information on a party's written request (with archival/backup retention carve-outs) and is not tied to occur after return/export, so it does not supply this element.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" — the assistance period and the export duty both attach to every covered expiry or termination event, satisfying the requirement that the period apply after every covered exit.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "provide Sanofi with reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination" — RevMed (counterparty) is the obligor and the floor is 90 days. The "at Sanofi's request" trigger is a general request condition, not one tied only to anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall, within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to Sanofi all data and materials of Sanofi then in RevMed's possession or control" — unconditional, correct temporal anchor, correct party direction.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (90-day floor, 30-day export, applies to any expiry or termination, obligor is RevMed). Preferred is not met — the clause lacks the six-month period, the then-current-rates anchor, the machine-readable format requirement, and the post-return certified-deletion step.

The finding's 'missing' classification is sound: existing 12.3(c)(vi)/(vi)C impose transition and transfer duties only on Sanofi; 12.3(e) is confined to one Change-of-Control termination scenario with bracketed, undisclosed scope; and 11.6 provides only request-based destruction of Confidential Information, not a fixed-period return/export to Sanofi.

Minimality holds: a single concise sentence inserted as 12.3(f), nothing deleted or paraphrased elsewhere, no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or boilerplate added. Note for the drafter: "and materials" marginally exceeds the data-export element; trimming to "all Sanofi data" would be tighter, but the phrase is a single deliverable formulation in this context and does not amount to a separate added requirement.

Intent preserved: the insertion is additive and reciprocal, uses only defined parties, creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict 12.3(e) (narrow CoC assistance) or 11.6 (which continues to govern destruction of Confidential Information on request).

If the client wants the preferred position, the repair is limited to four edits in 12.3(f): extend to "up to six (6) months", add "at RevMed's then-current rates", add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the export obligation, and add "and shall thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing" (sequenced after return).
